title: Throughput Tuner: Recommendation Journey for Batching & Cache
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design an end-to-end "Throughput Tuner" experience inside Redwood Console that recommends batching and cache configurations for a given route/model workload, explains expected latency/cost trade-offs, and enforces safety guardrails. Scope: recommendation panel (auto-suggested batch size, TTL, prefix caching choices), lightweight explainer copy & inline simulator, confidence meter, and an opt-in safe-mode that pins conservative settings. Excludes backend scheduler changes and autoscaling policy implementation (engineering will own the API contract). Goal: reduce time for engineers to tune throughput/cost from hours of manual testing to a guided 5-10 minute flow with measurable cost savings and no regression to latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive Throughput Tuner panel mock exists in Figma with primary flows: Preview, Accept Recommendation, Adjust, Enable Safe-mode
Recommendations are backed by a simple on-page simulator that shows estimated median latency change and cost delta for 'current', 'recommended', and 'aggressive' presets
Guardrail rules are surfaced when a recommended config risks violating latency SLO (>10% regression) or increasing error rate risk (based on synthetic probe heuristics)
Copy and inline help explain the reasoning behind each recommendation and what workload signals were used (batching ratio, seq len distribution, cache hit rate)
Design handoff includes component specs, accessibility notes, edge states, and QA checklist
PM and Eng have reviewed and approved the flow and provided the API contract snippet for the simulator inputs/outputs
decisions: Use three recommendation tiers: conservative, balanced (default), and aggressive — communicates risk vs. reward clearly
Include a confidence meter driven by historical traffic variance and sample size; low-confidence recommendations show a 'pilot' CTA instead of immediate apply
Expose an 'explain' flyout listing the key signals used (avg seq len, KV cache hit rate, per-request token distribution) rather than raw telemetry charts
Safe-mode will prevent any config change that simulation predicts will exceed user-configured latency SLO by >10%
Place the tuner as a per-route panel inside Route Settings, and surface a summary card on Route Overview when a recommendation exists
tradeoffs: Simulator accuracy vs. speed: We opted for a lightweight estimator that runs instantly in the browser using recent aggregated metrics rather than a full backend re-run — faster but less precise
UI surface complexity vs. clarity: limited advanced toggles in the first iteration to avoid overwhelming users; advanced mode postponed to a follow-up
Conservative default reduces potential cost savings but minimizes regression risk for first-time users
user_research_notes: 6 participants (platform engineers and ML infra) — participants liked a single recommended setting but wanted an easy way to run a short pilot
Participants were confused by raw metric names; preferred human-readable signal names ("avg prompt length" vs "avg_seq_len")
Confidence meter was repeatedly cited as the most useful single feature for trusting automated recommendations
Concerns raised about auditability: users wanted a changelog + reason attached to any applied recommendation
